title: Sentinel watch: Marketable Treasury securities held in custody for foreign official and international accounts
what_the_rule_says: Sentinels only report. Emergency powers need joint certification by the money authority head and the Treasury Secretary (Ch. 8).
who_decides: Money authority head and Treasury Secretary (emergency clause); Exchange Stabilization Fund (swap lines)

evidence.note: A fast fall means foreign official holders are selling or repo-ing Treasuries.

title: 6 rule interpretations awaiting a Design Paper ruling
what_happened: The shadow run had to choose how to implement details the book leaves open.
what_the_rule_says: The working specification is the Design Paper, which lists definitions and operating rules still to be completed (Ch. 7).
evidence: CPI-U and the PCE price index have different base years, so each is measured as a log gap from its own epoch level and the two gaps are averaged.
The seasonally adjusted CPI-U (CPIAUCSL) is used; the book says CPI-U without specifying seasonal adjustment.
The annual path rate is turned into a quarterly step by compounding: (1 + a)^(1/4) - 1.
Computation dates are fixed at the 15th of the second month after each quarter ends (Feb 15, May 15, Aug 15, Nov 15).
Trend real growth is the arithmetic mean of the last ten annual percent changes in real GDP available on the computation date.
Inputs come through FRED, which serves the latest revised figures. The design calls for figures as first released; vintage handling is a v2 task (ALFRED).

title: Transition dollar backstop: proposal awaiting review
what_happened: A capped, tapering, published dollar backstop for the switch-over has been proposed but is not part of the design.
what_the_rule_says: Foreign central-bank swap lines move to the Exchange Stabilization Fund: every line published, capped and time-limited (Ch. 8).
who_decides: Jamie, after Agent 2 and outside reviewers (e.g., offshore-dollar specialists)
evidence: Is a cap of 20% of foreign official custody holdings large enough? It would have covered the 2020 swap peak (about $449B) but not the 2008 peak (about $583B).
Should the taper follow the calendar, the sentinel readings, or both?
Which central banks are eligible, and who decides?
Does the design need any rule about dollar deposits created by banks outside the United States, or only a backstop?
